title: Medical Parasitology - Year 1 Fundamentals
description: Introductory medical parasitology covering protozoa, helminths, arthropod vectors, and parasitic diseases for Year 1 medical students.

questions.question_text: What is a parasite?
questions.explanation: A parasite is an organism that lives on or in a host, deriving nutrients at the host's expense.

answers.answer_text: An organism that lives on/in another organism and benefits at its expense
A beneficial organism in the gut

questions.question_text: Which parasite causes malaria?
questions.explanation: Plasmodium species (P. falciparum, P. vivax, P. ovale, P. malariae, P. knowlesi) cause malaria.

questions.question_text: What is the vector for malaria transmission?
questions.explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium parasites through their bite.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between a definitive host and an intermediate host?
questions.explanation: Definitive host harbors the adult/sexual stage; intermediate host harbors the larval/asexual stage.

answers.answer_text: Definitive host has adult/sexual stage; intermediate has larval/asexual stage
Intermediate host is where the parasite reproduces

questions.question_text: Which protozoan causes amoebic dysentery?
questions.explanation: Entamoeba histolytica causes amoebic dysentery (bloody diarrhea) and liver abscesses.

questions.question_text: What is the infective form of Entamoeba histolytica?
questions.explanation: The mature cyst is the infective form, transmitted via the fecal-oral route in contaminated food/water.

questions.question_text: Which parasite causes sleeping sickness?
questions.explanation: Trypanosoma brucei (T.b. gambiense and T.b. rhodesiense) causes African sleeping sickness.

questions.question_text: What type of organism is Ascaris lumbricoides?
questions.explanation: Ascaris lumbricoides is a roundworm (nematode) - the most common human intestinal helminth.

questions.question_text: Which parasite causes giardiasis?
questions.explanation: Giardia lamblia (G. intestinalis) causes giardiasis - a common cause of traveler's diarrhea.

questions.question_text: What is the vector for Chagas disease?
questions.explanation: Triatomine bugs (kissing bugs/reduviid bugs) transmit Trypanosoma cruzi, which causes Chagas disease.

questions.question_text: What type of parasite is Taenia solium?
questions.explanation: Taenia solium is a tapeworm (cestode) - the pork tapeworm that can cause cysticercosis.

questions.question_text: Which Plasmodium species causes the most severe form of malaria?
questions.explanation: P. falciparum causes the most severe malaria, including cerebral malaria, and is responsible for most deaths.

questions.question_text: What causes schistosomiasis (bilharzia)?
questions.explanation: Schistosoma species (blood flukes) cause schistosomiasis. Cercariae penetrate skin in contaminated water.

questions.question_text: What is the intermediate host for Schistosoma?
questions.explanation: Freshwater snails are the intermediate host where Schistosoma develops into cercariae.

questions.question_text: Which parasite causes leishmaniasis?
questions.explanation: Leishmania species cause leishmaniasis (cutaneous, mucocutaneous, or visceral forms).

questions.question_text: What is the vector for leishmaniasis?
questions.explanation: Sandflies (Phlebotomus and Lutzomyia species) transmit Leishmania parasites.

questions.question_text: Which parasite can cause neurocysticercosis?
questions.explanation: Taenia solium larvae (cysticerci) can migrate to the brain, causing neurocysticercosis - a major cause of seizures.

questions.question_text: What parasite causes toxoplasmosis?
questions.explanation: Toxoplasma gondii causes toxoplasmosis. Cats are the definitive host; humans are intermediate hosts.

questions.question_text: What is the definitive host for Toxoplasma gondii?
questions.explanation: Cats (felids) are the definitive host where T. gondii undergoes sexual reproduction.

questions.question_text: Which hookworm species infects humans?
questions.explanation: Ancylostoma duodenale and Necator americanus are the two main human hookworm species.

questions.question_text: How do hookworms typically infect humans?
questions.explanation: Hookworm larvae in soil penetrate bare skin (usually feet), then migrate to the intestines.

questions.question_text: What is elephantiasis caused by?
questions.explanation: Lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis) is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti and Brugia species (filarial worms).

questions.question_text: Which parasite causes river blindness?
questions.explanation: Onchocerca volvulus causes onchocerciasis (river blindness), transmitted by blackflies.

questions.question_text: What is the diagnostic stage of Plasmodium seen in blood smears?
questions.explanation: Ring-form trophozoites and later stages (schizonts, gametocytes) are seen in blood smears for malaria diagnosis.

questions.question_text: What is the main drug used to treat malaria caused by P. falciparum?
questions.explanation: Artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs) are the first-line treatment for P. falciparum malaria.
